ARC01 Avoid module dependency cycles · Architecture · 0 violations · 0 min

Modules that depend on each other, directly or through other modules, can only be understood, tested, built and released together. A cycle turns separate layers into one big tangle and every change risks rippling around the loop.

How to fix: Find the weakest edge of the cycle (fewest imports, shown in red) and remove it: move the shared code down into a lower module, or invert the dependency with an interface or callback owned by the lower module.

ARC03 Depend in the direction of stability · Architecture · 0 violations · 0 min

Stable dependencies principle: a module should only depend on modules that are more stable than itself. When a stable module (many dependents, few dependencies) depends on a clearly less stable one, changes in the volatile module ripple into everything that relies on the stable one.

How to fix: Move the code the stable module needs into it or into a lower module, or let the stable module define an abstraction that the volatile module implements.

ARC04 Modules in the zone of pain · Architecture · 0 violations · 0 min

A module that is concrete (few abstract types) and stable (used by many, depends on few) is hard to change because every dependent breaks, yet offers no abstractions to extend it. It sits far below the main sequence in the abstractness × instability diagram.

How to fix: Introduce interfaces or abstract types that dependents use instead of the concrete code, or split the module so that fewer modules depend on the concrete parts.

ARC05 Modules in the zone of uselessness · Architecture · 0 violations · 0 min

A module that is mostly abstract yet has no dependents is abstraction nobody uses: interfaces without callers, speculative extension points.

How to fix: Remove the unused abstractions, or merge them into the module that implements them.

DES01 Avoid hub files · Design · 0 violations · 0 min

A file that many files import and that itself imports many files is a hub: every change to its dependencies can break its many dependents. Hubs are usually god objects or grab-bag utility files.

How to fix: Split the file by responsibility so that each dependent imports only the part it needs.

DES02 Avoid too many imports in one file · Design · 0 violations · 0 min

A file with a very long import list knows too much about the rest of the system and is likely doing several jobs.

How to fix: Split the file along its responsibilities, or group related imports behind a facade.

CS03 Avoid deep nesting · Code smells · 0 violations · 0 min

Code nested more than five levels deep forces the reader to hold every enclosing condition in mind.

How to fix: Return early, invert conditions, and extract inner loops into their own functions.

CS05 Avoid brain methods · Code smells · 0 violations · 0 min

A brain method is long, complex and deeply nested at the same time: it centralizes the logic of its file and is where most bugs hide.

How to fix: Break it up step by step: extract each nested block into a named function, then simplify the remaining control flow.

MNT01 Avoid large files · Maintainability · 0 violations · 0 min

Files with more than 1,000 lines of code are hard to navigate and attract merge conflicts; above 2,000 lines they usually hold several unrelated concerns.

How to fix: Split the file by responsibility, one concept per file.

MNT04 Avoid knowledge islands · Maintainability · 0 violations · 0 min

One person wrote more than 90 % of a file that changes often. When they are away, nobody else knows the code.

How to fix: Pair on the next changes, review them with a second person, and write down how the file works.

ARC03 Depend in the direction of stability · Architecture · 0 violations · 0 min

Stable dependencies principle: a module should only depend on modules that are more stable than itself. When a stable module (many dependents, few dependencies) depends on a clearly less stable one, changes in the volatile module ripple into everything that relies on the stable one.

How to fix: Move the code the stable module needs into it or into a lower module, or let the stable module define an abstraction that the volatile module implements.

DES01 Avoid hub files · Design · 0 violations · 0 min

A file that many files import and that itself imports many files is a hub: every change to its dependencies can break its many dependents. Hubs are usually god objects or grab-bag utility files.

How to fix: Split the file by responsibility so that each dependent imports only the part it needs.

DES02 Avoid too many imports in one file · Design · 0 violations · 0 min

A file with a very long import list knows too much about the rest of the system and is likely doing several jobs.

How to fix: Split the file along its responsibilities, or group related imports behind a facade.
